Base directory for this skill: D:\code\codeflow\.claude\skills\cook # Cook - Smart Feature Implementation End-to-end implementation with automatic workflow detection. **Principles:** YAGNI, KISS, DRY | Token efficiency | Concise reports ## Usage ``` /ck:cook ``` **IMPORTANT:** If no flag is provided, the skill will use the `interactive` mode by default for the workflow. **Optional flags to select the workflow mode:** - `--interactive`: Full workflow with user input (**default**) - `--fast`: Skip research, scout→plan→code - `--parallel`: Multi-agent execution - `--no-test`: Skip testing step - `--auto`: Auto-approve all steps **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): - `--tdd`: Tests-first per phase — write tests for current behavior before refactoring, then verify they still pass after the implementation step **Example:** ``` /ck:cook "Add user authentication to the app" --fast /ck:cook path/to/plan.md --auto /ck:cook "Refactor auth middleware" --tdd ``` Do NOT write implementation code until a plan exists and has been reviewed. This applies regardless of task simplicity. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions waste the most time. Exception: `--fast` mode skips research but still requires a plan step. User override: If user explicitly says "just code it" or "skip planning", respect their instruction. Before planning OR asking clarifying questions, scan the codebase. Mandatory scout outputs: 1. Project type, language(s), framework(s) 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the task 3. Current patterns/conventions for similar features (so the implementation matches them) 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any in-flight plans in `./plans/` covering this area 5. Public APIs, schemas, contracts that the task could affect State a 3-6 bullet codebase-context summary to the user before asking questions. Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path (the plan already encodes scout output). Before producing a plan, you MUST be able to answer ALL of these in one concrete sentence each (use `AskUserQuestion` to pin them down — do NOT proceed on vague intent): 1. **Expected output**: the concrete artifact(s) the user will see at the end (file paths, feature behavior, UI screen, API endpoint + payload, CLI command + flags). 2. **Acceptance criteria**: specific behaviors / inputs → outputs / edge cases that MUST work to call it "done". 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope this round. 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines, performance. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will be modified or extended; which contracts must stay stable. Ground every `AskUserQuestion` option in scout findings (e.g., "Add to `src/api/users.ts` (matches existing pattern) or new `src/api/profile.ts`?"). Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path. Implementation is NOT done until verified to be side-effect-free. Code-review and test gates MUST prove: 1. New behavior matches every acceptance criterion above. 2. All tests pass — including tests in modules that share files/contracts with the change. 3. No existing business logic / workflow regression: explicitly walk each touchpoint and any caller of changed functions. 4. No new lint/type/build errors anywhere in the repo. 5. Public contracts unchanged unless intentional and called out (function signatures, exported types, API responses, DB schemas, env vars, config keys). User override: If user invoked `--no-test`, item 2 is downgraded to a warning. Surface the unverified-tests risk in the finalize `AskUserQuestion` so the user accepts the trade-off rather than having it silently chosen. Items 1, 3, 4, 5 remain enforceable via the mandatory `code-reviewer` subagent. If review/testing reveals a side effect, regression, or broken workflow, STOP. Use `AskUserQuestion` to present: - What broke (file, test, workflow, user-facing behavior) - Why this implementation caused it (1-line cause) - 2-4 concrete options for the user to choose, e.g.: - "Revert this slice and re-plan with stricter scope" - "Keep the implementation and update to match the new contract" - "Add a compatibility shim at so old callers keep working" - "Accept the regression — old behavior was unintended/buggy" Let the user decide. Do not silently patch around regressions. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to plan" | Simple tasks have hidden complexity. Plan takes 30 seconds. | | "I already know how to do this" | Knowing ≠ planning. Write it down. | | "Let me just start coding" | Undisciplined action wastes tokens. Plan first. | | "The user wants speed" | Fastest path = plan → implement → done. Not: implement → debug → rewrite. | | "I'll plan as I go" | That's not planning, that's hoping. | | "Just this once" | Every skip is "just this once." No exceptions. | ## Smart Intent Detection | Input Pattern | Detected Mode | Behavior | |---------------|---------------|----------| | Path to `plan.md` or `phase-*.md` | code | Execute existing plan | | Contains "fast", "quick" | fast | Skip research, scout→plan→code | | Contains "trust me", "auto" | auto | Auto-approve all steps | | Lists 3+ features OR "parallel" | parallel | Multi-agent execution | | Contains "no test", "skip test" | no-test | Skip testing step | | Default | interactive | Full workflow with user input | See `references/intent-detection.md` for detection logic. ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Intent Detection] --> B{Has plan path?} B -->|Yes| F[Load Plan] B -->|No| C{Mode?} C -->|fast| D[Scout → Plan → Code] C -->|interactive/auto| SC[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] SC --> SR[Summarize Findings to User] SR --> RQ{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} RQ -->|No| SR RQ -->|Yes| E[Research → Review → Plan] E --> F D --> F F --> G[Review Gate] G -->|approved| H[Implement] G -->|rejected| E H --> H1{Simplify signal?} H1 -->|Yes| H2[Conditional Simplify] H1 -->|No| I[Review Gate] H2 --> I I -->|approved| J{--no-test?} J -->|No| K[Test] J -->|Yes| L[Finalize] K --> L L --> M[Report + Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. ## Workflow Overview ``` [Intent Detection] → [Research?] → [Review] → [Plan] → [Review] → [Implement] → [Conditional Simplify?] → [Review] → [Test?] → [Review] → [Finalize] ``` **Default (non-auto):** Stops at `[Review]` gates for human approval before each major step. **Auto mode (`--auto`):** Skips human review gates, implements all phases continuously. **Claude Tasks:** Utilize `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList` during implementation step. **Fallback:** These are CLI-only tools — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for progress tracking instead. | Mode | Research | Testing | Review Gates | Phase Progression | |------|----------|---------|--------------|-------------------| | interactive | ✓ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | auto | ✓ | ✓ | Auto if score≥9.5 | All at once (no stops) | | fast | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | parallel | Optional | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Parallel groups | | no-test | ✓ | ✗ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | code | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Per plan | ## Step Output Format ``` ✓ Step [N]: [Brief status] - [Key metrics] ``` ## Blocking Gates (Non-Auto Mode) Human review required at these checkpoints (skipped with `--auto`): - **Post-Research:** Review findings before planning - **Post-Plan:** Approve plan before implementation - **Post-Implementation:** Approve code before testing - **Post-Testing:** 100% pass + approve before finalize **Always enforced (all modes):** - **Testing:** 100% pass required (unless no-test mode) - **Code Review (MANDATORY):** Spawn `code-reviewer` subagent with explicit checks: (a) every acceptance criterion met, (b) no regression to business logic in touchpoints/blast-radius, (c) no breaking changes to public contracts (signatures, schemas, APIs, env vars) unless called out, (d) follows existing patterns from scout, (e) no new lint/type/build errors anywhere. Pass scout summary + acceptance criteria as context. If reviewer flags side effects → trigger HARD-GATE-NO-SIDE-EFFECTS (`AskUserQuestion` with 2-4 options). Then: User approval OR auto-approve (score≥9.5, 0 critical). - **Finalize (MANDATORY - never skip):** 1. **Activate `/ck:project-management` skill (MANDATORY)** → run full plan sync-back across ALL `phase-XX-*.md` (not only current phase), update `plan.md` status/progress, hydrate Claude Tasks, generate progress report 2. `docs-manager` subagent → update `./docs` if changes warrant 3. `TaskUpdate` → mark all Claude Tasks complete after sync-back verification (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Ask user if they want to commit via `git-manager` subagent 5. Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ## Required Subagents (MANDATORY) | Phase | Subagent | Requirement | |-------|----------|-------------| | Research | `researcher` | Optional in fast/code | | Scout | `ck:scout` | Optional in code | | Plan | `planner` | Optional in code | | UI Work | `ui-ux-designer` | If frontend work | | Testing | `tester`, `debugger` | **MUST** spawn | | Review | `code-reviewer` | **MUST** spawn | | Finalize | `/ck:project-management` skill + `docs-manager`, `git-manager` subagents | **MUST** invoke all | **CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT:** - Steps 4, 5, 6 **MUST** use Task tool to spawn subagents - DO NOT implement testing, review, or finalization yourself - DELEGATE - If workflow ends with 0 Task tool calls, it is INCOMPLETE - Pattern: `Task(subagent_type="[type]", prompt="[task]", description="[brief]")` ## References - `references/intent-detection.md` - Detection rules and routing logic - `references/workflow-steps.md` - Detailed step definitions for all modes - `references/review-cycle.md` - Interactive and auto review processes - `references/subagent-patterns.md` - Subagent invocation patterns ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:plan` (execute a plan), `/ck:brainstorm` (implement agreed solution) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:code-review` (review after implementation), `/ck:test` (validate changes) **Related:** `/ck:fix` (alternative for bug fixes), `/ck:plan` (create plan before cooking) ARGUMENTS: plans/260605-investor-demo-stack/plan.md

# Phase 1: Dashboard Auth Bypass

## Overview

WorkOS AuthKit middleware throws 500 on every request when `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` is not set. Add dev-mode bypass so dashboard works locally without WorkOS credentials.

**Root cause:** `middleware.ts` calls `authkitMiddleware()` which requires `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI` env var. Without it → hard crash.

**NOTE:** Next.js 16.2.7 shows deprecation warning: "middleware file convention is deprecated, use proxy instead". We keep `middleware.ts` for now since AuthKit SDK depends on it — migration to `proxy` is out of scope.

## Requirements

- Functional: Dashboard loads at `localhost:3000` without any WorkOS env vars set
- Functional: When WorkOS vars ARE set, auth works normally (no regression)
- Non-functional: Zero additional dependencies

## Architecture

```
Request → middleware.ts
  ├─ CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true → passthrough (no auth)
  └─ WorkOS vars set → authkitMiddleware() (existing flow)
```

For components that call `useAuth()` from WorkOS SDK: conditionally return mock user when auth disabled.

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `dashboard/src/middleware.ts` — conditional bypass
- Modify: `dashboard/src/app/layout.tsx` — conditional `<AuthKitProvider>`
- Modify: `dashboard/src/components/user-nav.tsx` — graceful fallback when no auth
- Modify: `dashboard/src/app/auth/callback/route.ts` — guard against missing WorkOS
- Modify: `dashboard/.env.local` — add `CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true`

## Implementation Steps

1. **`dashboard/src/middleware.ts`** — Add bypass before authkitMiddleware:
   ```ts
   import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
   import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
   
   export default function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
     if (process.env.CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED === "true") {
       return NextResponse.next();
     }
     // Dynamic import to avoid crash when WorkOS vars missing
     const { authkitMiddleware } = require("@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs");
     return authkitMiddleware({
       middlewareAuth: {
         enabled: true,
         unauthenticatedPaths: ["/auth/callback"],
       },
     })(request);
   }
   ```
   
   **Note:** Dynamic require avoids the SDK crashing at import time when env vars are missing. Alternative: use `next/dynamic` pattern. Test both — if dynamic require doesn't work in edge middleware, fall back to try/catch wrapper.

2. **`dashboard/src/app/layout.tsx`** — Conditionally wrap with AuthKitProvider:
   ```tsx
   // If auth disabled, skip AuthKitProvider entirely
   // Use a server component check on process.env
   ```
   Since `layout.tsx` is a server component, read `process.env.CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED` directly. When true, render children without `<AuthKitProvider>`.

3. **`dashboard/src/components/user-nav.tsx`** — Handle missing auth context:
   ```tsx
   // When auth disabled, show "Demo Mode" instead of user info
   // Don't call useAuth() when provider is not mounted
   ```
   Wrap `useAuth()` call in try-catch or use a context check. When auth disabled, show static "Demo User" / "demo@codeflow.dev".

4. **`dashboard/src/app/auth/callback/route.ts`** — Guard:
   ```ts
   // When CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true, redirect to / immediately
   ```

5. **`dashboard/.env.local`** — Add:
   ```
   CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true
   ```

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `npm run dev` starts without errors (no WorkOS crash)
- [ ] `curl localhost:3000` returns 200 (not 500)
- [ ] All 7 pages accessible in browser
- [ ] UserNav shows "Demo Mode" or similar
- [ ] Auth callback redirects to / gracefully
- [ ] `next build` succeeds

## Risk Assessment

- **Edge middleware limitations:** Next.js edge middleware may not support `require()`. Mitigation: use conditional export pattern or move auth check to a wrapper function.
- **AuthKit context missing:** Components using `useAuth()` will throw if `<AuthKitProvider>` not mounted. Mitigation: wrap in error boundary or conditional component.
- **Regression risk:** Changes to middleware could break production auth. Mitigation: all changes gated behind `CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED` env var — production never sets this.

## Overview

## Requirements

- Functional: `docker compose run seed` populates ClickHouse with 570+ demo events
- Functional: Seed runs after migrate and ingest are healthy
- Non-functional: Seed container exits cleanly after completion

## Architecture

```
docker-compose up
  └─ seed service (depends_on: ingest healthy)
       └─ POST http://ingest:8080/v1/events (protobuf+gzip)
            └─ X-Tenant-ID: demo-tenant
```

The seed script already sends the correct `X-Tenant-ID: demo-tenant` header and targets `localhost:8080`. In Docker, it needs to target `ingest:8080` instead.

## Related Code Files

- Create: `cloud/Dockerfile.seed` — multi-stage build for seed binary
- Modify: `cloud/docker-compose.yml` — add `seed` service
- Modify: `cloud/cmd/seed/main.go` — use env var for API URL (currently hardcoded to `localhost:8080`)

## Implementation Steps

1. **`cloud/cmd/seed/main.go`** — Make API URL configurable:
   ```go
   // Replace hardcoded "http://localhost:8080/v1/events" with:
   apiURL := os.Getenv("CODEFLOW_API_URL")
   if apiURL == "" {
       apiURL = "http://localhost:8080"
   }
   req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", apiURL+"/v1/events", &buf)
   ```

2. **`cloud/Dockerfile.seed`** — Multi-stage build:
   ```dockerfile
   FROM golang:1.25-alpine AS build
   WORKDIR /app
   COPY go.mod go.sum ./
   RUN go mod download
   COPY . .
   RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o /seed ./cmd/seed
   
   FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot

   ```yaml

       context: .
       dockerfile: Dockerfile.seed
     environment:
       CODEFLOW_API_URL: "http://ingest:8080"

       ingest:
         condition: service_healthy

     timeout: 3s

   - Switch to alpine-based final stage for ingest
   - Use `httpGet`-style check via a tiny Go binary

# Phase 3: Root Docker Compose

## Overview

Create a root `docker-compose.yml` that orchestrates the full stack: ClickHouse + NATS + Go API + seed data + Next.js dashboard. Single `docker compose up` from repo root starts everything needed for investor demo.

## Requirements

- Functional: `docker compose up` from repo root starts all services
- Functional: Dashboard accessible at `http://localhost:3000` with seed data
- Functional: API accessible at `http://localhost:8080`
- Non-functional: Full stack healthy within 90s

## Architecture

```
docker-compose.yml (repo root)
├── clickhouse (port 9000, 8123)
├── nats (port 4222)
├── migrate (depends: clickhouse)
├── ingest (port 8080, depends: clickhouse, nats, migrate)
├── writer (depends: clickhouse, nats, migrate)
├── seed (depends: ingest, profile: seed)
└── dashboard (port 3000, depends: ingest)
```

## Related Code Files

- Create: `docker-compose.yml` (repo root) — full stack orchestration
- Create: `dashboard/Dockerfile` — multi-stage Next.js build
- Modify: `cloud/docker-compose.yml` — keep as standalone backend-only option

## Implementation Steps

1. **`dashboard/Dockerfile`** — Multi-stage Next.js build:
   ```dockerfile
   FROM node:22-alpine AS deps
   WORKDIR /app
   COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
   RUN npm ci
   
   FROM node:22-alpine AS build
   WORKDIR /app
   COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
   COPY . .
   ENV CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true
   ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
   ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_TENANT_ID=demo-tenant
   RUN npm run build
   
   FROM node:22-alpine
   WORKDIR /app
   COPY --from=build /app/.next ./.next
   COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
   COPY --from=build /app/package.json ./
   COPY --from=build /app/public ./public
   ENV NODE_ENV=production
   ENV CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED=true
   EXPOSE 3000
   CMD ["npm", "start"]
   ```
   
   **Critical:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars must be set at BUILD time for Next.js (they're inlined during build). `CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED` is read at runtime by middleware.

2. **Root `docker-compose.yml`** — Include all services:
   ```yaml
   services:
     clickhouse:
       image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8
       ports: ["8123:8123", "9000:9000"]
       volumes: [clickhouse-data:/var/lib/clickhouse]
       environment:
         CLICKHOUSE_DEFAULT_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT: 1
       ulimits:
         nofile: {soft: 262144, hard: 262144}
       healthcheck:
         test: ["CMD", "clickhouse-client", "--query", "SELECT 1"]
         interval: 5s
         timeout: 3s
         retries: 10

     nats:
       image: nats:2.10-alpine
       command: ["--jetstream", "--store_dir", "/data"]
       ports: ["4222:4222"]
       volumes: [nats-data:/data]
       healthcheck:
         test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "nc -z localhost 4222 || exit 1"]
         interval: 5s
         timeout: 3s
         retries: 10
         start_period: 5s

     migrate:
       build: {context: ./cloud, dockerfile: Dockerfile.migrate}
       environment:
         CLICKHOUSE_DSN: "clickhouse://clickhouse:9000/"
       depends_on:
         clickhouse: {condition: service_healthy}

     ingest:
       build: ./cloud
       ports: ["8080:8080"]
       environment:
         CLICKHOUSE_DSN: "clickhouse://clickhouse:9000/codeflow"
         NATS_URL: "nats://nats:4222"
         LISTEN_ADDR: ":8080"
         CORS_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:3000"
         CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED: "true"
       depends_on:
         clickhouse: {condition: service_healthy}
         nats: {condition: service_healthy}
         migrate: {condition: service_completed_successfully}

     writer:
       build: {context: ./cloud, dockerfile: Dockerfile.writer}
       environment:
         CLICKHOUSE_DSN: "clickhouse://clickhouse:9000/codeflow"
         NATS_URL: "nats://nats:4222"
         CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED: "true"
       depends_on:
         clickhouse: {condition: service_healthy}
         nats: {condition: service_healthy}
         migrate: {condition: service_completed_successfully}

     seed:
       build: {context: ./cloud, dockerfile: Dockerfile.seed}
       environment:
         CODEFLOW_API_URL: "http://ingest:8080"
       depends_on:
         ingest: {condition: service_started}
       profiles: [seed]

     dashboard:
       build: ./dashboard
       ports: ["3000:3000"]
       environment:
         CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED: "true"
         NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: "http://localhost:8080"
         NEXT_PUBLIC_TENANT_ID: "demo-tenant"
       depends_on:
         ingest: {condition: service_started}

   volumes:
     clickhouse-data:
     nats-data:
   ```

3. **Keep `cloud/docker-compose.yml`** as-is for backend-only development. Add comment at top:
   ```yaml
   # Backend-only stack. For full stack (incl. dashboard), use root docker-compose.yml
   ```

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `docker compose up` from repo root builds all images
- [ ] All services reach healthy/running state
- [ ] Dashboard accessible at `http://localhost:3000`
- [ ] API accessible at `http://localhost:8080/healthz`
- [ ] `docker compose --profile seed up seed` populates data

## Risk Assessment

- **Build time:** First build downloads Go modules + npm packages. ~3-5 min. Acceptable for setup.
- **NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time:** Next.js inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` during build. The Docker build sets them, but they won't match if user changes ports. Mitigation: document this limitation.
- **Port conflicts:** 3000, 8080, 8123, 9000, 4222 must be free. Mitigation: document required ports.
- **Dashboard API calls:** Browser makes requests to `localhost:8080` (not Docker network). CORS must allow `localhost:3000` origin — already configured via `CORS_ORIGIN` env var.

17		events := make([]*pb.Event, 0, 50)
18	
19		commands := []struct {
20			cmd    string
21			filter string
22			input  uint64
23			saved  uint64
24		}{
25			{"git diff", "git-diff", 8000, 3200},
26			{"git status", "git-status", 2000, 1400},
27			{"cargo test", "cargo-test", 12000, 5400},
28			{"npm test", "npm-test", 6000, 2100},
29			{"tsc", "tsc", 3000, 900},
30			{"cargo build", "cargo-build", 15000, 7500},
31			{"eslint .", "eslint", 4000, 1600},
32			{"pytest", "pytest", 5000, 1750},
33			{"go test ./...", "go-test", 9000, 3600},
34			{"docker logs app", "docker-logs", 7000, 4200},
35		}
36	
37		projects := []string{
38			"/home/user/codeflow",
39			"/home/user/dashboard",
40			"/home/user/api-server",
41		}
42	
43		id := 0
44		for day := 0; day < 14; day++ {
45			ts := now.AddDate(0, 0, -day)
46			for _, proj := range projects {
47				for _, cmd := range commands {
48					id++
49					events = append(events, &pb.Event{
50						Id:          fmt.Sprintf("seed-%d", id),
51						TimestampMs: ts.UnixMilli(),
52						SessionId:   fmt.Sprintf("sess-%d-%d", day, id%5),
53						ProjectDir:  proj,
54						Command:     cmd.cmd,
55						Compression: &pb.CompressionEvent{
56							InputBytes:  cmd.input * 4,
57							OutputBytes: (cmd.input - cmd.saved) * 4,
58							InputTokens: cmd.input,
59							OutputTokens: cmd.input - cmd.saved,
60							TokensSaved: cmd.saved,
61							FilterName:  cmd.filter,
62							LatencyMs:   1.5,
63						},
64					})
65	
66					if day%3 == 0 {
67						id++
68						events = append(events, &pb.Event{
69							Id:          fmt.Sprintf("seed-%d", id),
70							TimestampMs: ts.UnixMilli(),
71							SessionId:   fmt.Sprintf("sess-%d-%d", day, id%5),
72							ProjectDir:  proj,
73							Command:     cmd.cmd,
74							Dedup: &pb.DedupEvent{
75								ContentHash: fmt.Sprintf("hash-%d", id),
76								CacheHit:    true,
77								TokensSaved: cmd.saved / 2,
78								LatencyMs:   0.3,
79							},
80						})
81					}
82				}
83			}
84		}
85	
86		batch := &pb.EventBatch{
87			CliVersion: "0.1.0-seed",
88			MachineId:  "seed-machine",
89			Events:     events,
90		}
91	
92		data, err := proto.Marshal(batch)
93		if err != nil {
94			panic(err)
95		}
96	
97		var buf bytes.Buffer
98		gz := gzip.NewWriter(&buf)
99		gz.Write(data)
100		gz.Close()
101	
102		fmt.Printf("Seeding %d events (%d bytes proto, %d bytes gzipped)...\n",
103			len(events), len(data), buf.Len())
104	
105		req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "http://localhost:8080/v1/events", &buf)
106		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-protobuf")
107		req.Header.Set("Content-Encoding", "gzip")
108		req.Header.Set("X-Tenant-ID", "demo-tenant")
109	
110		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
111		if err != nil {
112			panic(err)
113		}
114		defer resp.Body.Close()
115	
116		body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
117		fmt.Printf("Response: %d %s\n", resp.StatusCode, string(body))
118	}

file.content:
services:
  nats:
    image: nats:2.10-alpine
    command: ["--jetstream", "--store_dir", "/data"]
    ports:
      - "4222:4222"
      - "8222:8222"
    volumes:
      - nats-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "nc -z localhost 4222 || exit 1"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 5s

  clickhouse:
    image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8
    ports:
      - "8123:8123"
      - "9000:9000"
    volumes:
      - clickhouse-data:/var/lib/clickhouse
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_DEFAULT_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT: 1
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 262144
        hard: 262144
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "clickhouse-client", "--query", "SELECT 1"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  migrate:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.migrate
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_DSN: "clickhouse://clickhouse:9000/"
    depends_on:
      clickhouse:
        condition: service_healthy

  ingest:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_DSN: "clickhouse://clickhouse:9000/codeflow"
      NATS_URL: "nats://nats:4222"
      LISTEN_ADDR: ":8080"
      CORS_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:3000"
      CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED: "true"
    depends_on:
      clickhouse:
        condition: service_healthy
      nats:
        condition: service_healthy
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  writer:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.writer
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_DSN: "clickhouse://clickhouse:9000/codeflow"
      NATS_URL: "nats://nats:4222"
      CODEFLOW_AUTH_DISABLED: "true"
    depends_on:
      clickhouse:
        condition: service_healthy
      nats:
        condition: service_healthy
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

volumes:
  clickhouse-data:
  nats-data:

1	# CODEFLOW
2	
3	**AI coding cost intelligence engine.** Reduce token costs 40-65% while proving developer productivity is maintained.
4	
5	CODEFLOW intercepts AI coding tool output, compresses it via smart filters, deduplicates repeated reads, and tracks savings — all with <5ms overhead.
6	
7	## Quick Start
8	
9	```bash
10	# Install
11	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow/main/install.sh | sh
12	
13	# Or with cargo
14	cargo install --git https://github.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow codeflow --root ~/.local
15	
16	# Set up hooks for Claude Code
17	codeflow init
18	
19	# View your savings
20	codeflow stats
21	```
22	
23	## How It Works
24	
25	CODEFLOW installs as a Claude Code hook that intercepts **all major tool calls** — Bash, Read, Grep, and Glob:
26	
27	```
28	Claude Code → PreToolUse hook → codeflow processes → compressed/deduped output
29	```
30	
31	**Layer 1 — Compression:** An 8-stage TOML filter pipeline strips noise from Bash command output:
32	- ANSI codes, download progress bars, empty lines
33	- Verbose compiler/test output condensed to errors + summary
34	- Long outputs truncated with head/tail
35	
36	**Layer 2 — Dedup:** Content-addressed cache detects repeated Bash command output within a session and returns a one-line summary instead of full content.
37	
38	**Layer 2.5 — Read Dedup:** Intercepts Read/Grep/Glob tool calls. If a file was recently read and hasn't changed (mtime verified), injects `additionalContext` telling Claude the file is unchanged — saving 30-50% of session tokens from re-reads.
39	
40	**Session Context:** Every tool call is logged per-session (SQLite WAL, <1ms writes). This powers dedup checks and waste detection.
41	
42	**Waste Detection:** Analyzes session tool logs to surface waste patterns — files read 8x, identical greps, failed searches, glob spam.
43	
44	**Tracking:** Every compression and dedup event is logged locally (SQLite, 90-day retention) so you can see exactly how many tokens you're saving.
45	
46	## Filters
47	
48	15 built-in TOML filters for common commands:
49	
50	| Command | What it strips |
51	|---------|---------------|
52	| `git diff` | Index lines, no-newline markers, truncates long lines |
53	| `git status` | Hint text, compact modified/added/deleted prefixes |
54	| `git log` | Empty lines, truncates to 200 lines |
55	| `cargo build/test` | Compiling/Downloading lines, timing normalization |
56	| `npm test` | Warnings, stack traces, PASS/FAIL symbols |
57	| `pytest` | Warnings summary, site-packages paths |
58	| `tsc` | Empty lines, truncated long error lines |
59	| `eslint` | Empty lines, problem count summaries |
60	| `docker logs` | Timestamps stripped, head/tail |
61	| `go test` | PASS/FAIL symbols, timing normalization |
62	| `pip install` | Download/cache lines, collecting lines |
63	| `find` | Permission denied errors, head/tail |
64	| `grep` | Binary match lines, truncated long lines |
65	| `ls` | Total line, head/tail for large directories |
66	
67	### Custom Filters
68	
69	Create TOML files in `~/.local/share/codeflow/filters/`:
70	
71	```toml
72	strip_ansi = true
73	on_empty = "(no output)"
74	
75	[command]
76	name = "mycommand"
77	args_contain = ["--verbose"]
78	
79	[[strip_lines]]
80	pattern = '^DEBUG:'
81	
82	[head_tail]
83	head = 20
84	tail = 10
85	separator = "\n... ({omitted} lines omitted) ...\n"
86	
87	max_lines = 100
88	```
89	
90	## Commands
91	
92	```
93	codeflow init [-g]              Install hooks (project or global)
94	codeflow uninit [-g]            Remove hooks
95	codeflow wrap <cmd> [args]      Manually compress a command
96	codeflow stats [--json]         Show savings dashboard

# CODEFLOW

**AI coding cost intelligence engine.** Reduce token costs 40-65% while proving developer productivity is maintained.

CODEFLOW intercepts AI coding tool output, compresses it via smart filters, deduplicates repeated reads, and tracks savings — all with <5ms overhead.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow/main/install.sh | sh

# Or with cargo
cargo install --git https://github.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow codeflow --root ~/.local

# Set up hooks for Claude Code
codeflow init

# View your savings
codeflow stats
```

## How It Works

CODEFLOW installs as a Claude Code hook that intercepts **all major tool calls** — Bash, Read, Grep, and Glob:

```
Claude Code → PreToolUse hook → codeflow processes → compressed/deduped output
```

**Layer 1 — Compression:** An 8-stage TOML filter pipeline strips noise from Bash command output:
- ANSI codes, download progress bars, empty lines
- Verbose compiler/test output condensed to errors + summary
- Long outputs truncated with head/tail

**Layer 2 — Dedup:** Content-addressed cache detects repeated Bash command output within a session and returns a one-line summary instead of full content.

**Layer 2.5 — Read Dedup:** Intercepts Read/Grep/Glob tool calls. If a file was recently read and hasn't changed (mtime verified), injects `additionalContext` telling Claude the file is unchanged — saving 30-50% of session tokens from re-reads.

**Session Context:** Every tool call is logged per-session (SQLite WAL, <1ms writes). This powers dedup checks and waste detection.

**Waste Detection:** Analyzes session tool logs to surface waste patterns — files read 8x, identical greps, failed searches, glob spam.

**Tracking:** Every compression and dedup event is logged locally (SQLite, 90-day retention) so you can see exactly how many tokens you're saving.

## Filters

15 built-in TOML filters for common commands:

| Command | What it strips |
|---------|---------------|
| `git diff` | Index lines, no-newline markers, truncates long lines |
| `git status` | Hint text, compact modified/added/deleted prefixes |
| `git log` | Empty lines, truncates to 200 lines |
| `cargo build/test` | Compiling/Downloading lines, timing normalization |
| `npm test` | Warnings, stack traces, PASS/FAIL symbols |
| `pytest` | Warnings summary, site-packages paths |
| `tsc` | Empty lines, truncated long error lines |
| `eslint` | Empty lines, problem count summaries |
| `docker logs` | Timestamps stripped, head/tail |
| `go test` | PASS/FAIL symbols, timing normalization |
| `pip install` | Download/cache lines, collecting lines |
| `find` | Permission denied errors, head/tail |
| `grep` | Binary match lines, truncated long lines |
| `ls` | Total line, head/tail for large directories |

### Custom Filters

Create TOML files in `~/.local/share/codeflow/filters/`:

```toml
strip_ansi = true
on_empty = "(no output)"

[command]
name = "mycommand"
args_contain = ["--verbose"]

[[strip_lines]]
pattern = '^DEBUG:'

[head_tail]
head = 20
tail = 10
separator = "\n... ({omitted} lines omitted) ...\n"

max_lines = 100
```

## Commands

```
codeflow init [-g]              Install hooks (project or global)
codeflow uninit [-g]            Remove hooks
codeflow wrap <cmd> [args]      Manually compress a command
codeflow stats [--json]         Show savings dashboard
codeflow stats --waste [--json] Show waste pattern analysis
codeflow cache clear            Clear dedup cache
codeflow cache info             Show cache statistics
codeflow sync [--once]          Sync events to cloud (Phase 2)
codeflow update                 Show version and update info
```

## Fail-Open Design

Any internal error → original output passed unchanged. CODEFLOW never breaks your workflow:
- Invalid hook input → passthrough + stderr warning
- Filter crash → original output returned
- Database error → output still works, event not logged

## Architecture

```
cli/                    Rust workspace
├── crates/core/        Compression, dedup, events, tracking
├── crates/cli/         Binary, hooks, stats, sync
├── filters/            TOML filter definitions
└── proto/              Protobuf event schema

cloud/                  Go ingest server (Phase 2)
├── cmd/ingest/         HTTP server
└── internal/           ClickHouse client, API handlers

dashboard/              Next.js + React (Phase 2)
└── src/                Overview, settings pages
```

## Development

```bash
# Build
cd cli && cargo build

# Test (57 unit + 14 integration)
cd cli && cargo test

# Run locally
cd cli && cargo run -- wrap git status
```

## License

Apache-2.0

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# CODEFLOW

**AI coding cost intelligence engine.** Reduce token costs 40-65% while proving developer productivity is maintained.

CODEFLOW intercepts AI coding tool output, compresses it via smart filters, deduplicates repeated reads, and tracks savings — all with <5ms overhead.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow/main/install.sh | sh

# Or with cargo
cargo install --git https://github.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow codeflow --root ~/.local

# Set up hooks for Claude Code
codeflow init

# View your savings
codeflow stats
```

## How It Works

CODEFLOW installs as a Claude Code hook that intercepts **all major tool calls** — Bash, Read, Grep, and Glob:

```
Claude Code → PreToolUse hook → codeflow processes → compressed/deduped output
```

**Layer 1 — Compression:** An 8-stage TOML filter pipeline strips noise from Bash command output:
- ANSI codes, download progress bars, empty lines
- Verbose compiler/test output condensed to errors + summary
- Long outputs truncated with head/tail

**Layer 2 — Dedup:** Content-addressed cache detects repeated Bash command output within a session and returns a one-line summary instead of full content.

**Layer 2.5 — Read Dedup:** Intercepts Read/Grep/Glob tool calls. If a file was recently read and hasn't changed (mtime verified), injects `additionalContext` telling Claude the file is unchanged — saving 30-50% of session tokens from re-reads.

**Session Context:** Every tool call is logged per-session (SQLite WAL, <1ms writes). This powers dedup checks and waste detection.

**Waste Detection:** Analyzes session tool logs to surface waste patterns — files read 8x, identical greps, failed searches, glob spam.

**Tracking:** Every compression and dedup event is logged locally (SQLite, 90-day retention) so you can see exactly how many tokens you're saving.

## Filters

15 built-in TOML filters for common commands:

| Command | What it strips |
|---------|---------------|
| `git diff` | Index lines, no-newline markers, truncates long lines |
| `git status` | Hint text, compact modified/added/deleted prefixes |
| `git log` | Empty lines, truncates to 200 lines |
| `cargo build/test` | Compiling/Downloading lines, timing normalization |
| `npm test` | Warnings, stack traces, PASS/FAIL symbols |
| `pytest` | Warnings summary, site-packages paths |
| `tsc` | Empty lines, truncated long error lines |
| `eslint` | Empty lines, problem count summaries |
| `docker logs` | Timestamps stripped, head/tail |
| `go test` | PASS/FAIL symbols, timing normalization |
| `pip install` | Download/cache lines, collecting lines |
| `find` | Permission denied errors, head/tail |
| `grep` | Binary match lines, truncated long lines |
| `ls` | Total line, head/tail for large directories |

### Custom Filters

Create TOML files in `~/.local/share/codeflow/filters/`:

```toml
strip_ansi = true
on_empty = "(no output)"

[command]
name = "mycommand"
args_contain = ["--verbose"]

[[strip_lines]]
pattern = '^DEBUG:'

[head_tail]
head = 20
tail = 10
separator = "\n... ({omitted} lines omitted) ...\n"

max_lines = 100
```

## Commands

```
codeflow init [-g]              Install hooks (project or global)
codeflow uninit [-g]            Remove hooks
codeflow wrap <cmd> [args]      Manually compress a command
codeflow stats [--json]         Show savings dashboard
codeflow stats --waste [--json] Show waste pattern analysis
codeflow cache clear            Clear dedup cache
codeflow cache info             Show cache statistics
codeflow sync [--once]          Sync events to cloud (Phase 2)
codeflow update                 Show version and update info
```

## Fail-Open Design

Any internal error → original output passed unchanged. CODEFLOW never breaks your workflow:
- Invalid hook input → passthrough + stderr warning
- Filter crash → original output returned
- Database error → output still works, event not logged

## Architecture

```
cli/                    Rust workspace
├── crates/core/        Compression, dedup, events, tracking
├── crates/cli/         Binary, hooks, stats, sync
├── filters/            TOML filter definitions
└── proto/              Protobuf event schema

cloud/                  Go ingest server (Phase 2)
├── cmd/ingest/         HTTP server
└── internal/           ClickHouse client, API handlers

dashboard/              Next.js + React (Phase 2)
└── src/                Overview, settings pages
```

## Development

```bash
# Build
cd cli && cargo build

# Test (57 unit + 14 integration)
cd cli && cargo test

# Run locally
cd cli && cargo run -- wrap git status
```

## License

**Location:** `/d/code/codeflow`  
**Type:** Multi-component AI coding cost intelligence engine

## PROJECT OVERVIEW

CODEFLOW is a token cost optimizer for AI coding workflows. It:
- Intercepts Claude Code tool calls (Bash, Read, Grep, Glob) via pre/post hooks
- Compresses output via 15 built-in TOML filters + custom filter pipeline
- Deduplicates repeated file reads and command outputs within sessions
- Tracks savings locally (SQLite) and syncs to cloud dashboard
- **Target savings:** 40-65% token reduction with zero workflow disruption
- **Fail-open design:** Any error passes output unchanged

## PROJECT OVERVIEW

CODEFLOW is a token cost optimizer for AI coding workflows. It:

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  cli:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy

      - name: Install protoc
        uses: arduino/setup-protoc@v3
        with:
          version: "27.x"

      - name: Check
        working-directory: cli
        run: cargo check --locked

      - name: Clippy
        working-directory: cli
        run: cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        working-directory: cli
        run: cargo test --locked

  cloud:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.24"

      - name: Build
        working-directory: cloud
        run: go build ./...

      - name: Vet
        working-directory: cloud
        run: go vet ./...

      - name: Test
        working-directory: cloud
        run: go test ./... -count=1

  dashboard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Install
        working-directory: dashboard
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        working-directory: dashboard
        run: npx next lint

      - name: Type check
        working-directory: dashboard
        run: npx tsc --noEmit

      - name: Build
        working-directory: dashboard
        run: npx next build

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\codeflow\.claude\skills\brainstorm # Brainstorming Skill You are a Solution Brainstormer, an elite software engineering expert who specializes in system architecture design and technical decision-making. Your core mission is to collaborate with users to find the best possible solutions while maintaining brutal honesty about feasibility and trade-offs. ## Communication Style If coding level guidelines were injected at session start (levels 0-5), follow those guidelines for response structure and explanation depth. The guidelines define what to explain, what not to explain, and required response format. ## Core Principles You operate by the holy trinity of software engineering: **YAGNI** (You Aren't Gonna Need It), **KISS** (Keep It Simple, Stupid), and **DRY** (Don't Repeat Yourself). Every solution you propose must honor these principles. ## Your Expertise - System architecture design and scalability patterns - Risk assessment and mitigation strategies - Development time optimization and resource allocation - User Experience (UX) and Developer Experience (DX) optimization - Technical debt management and maintainability - Performance optimization and bottleneck identification ## Your Approach 1. **Question Everything**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask probing questions to fully understand the user's request, constraints, and true objectives. Don't assume - clarify until you're 100% certain. 2. **Brutal Honesty**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to provide frank, unfiltered feedback about ideas. If something is unrealistic, over-engineered, or likely to cause problems, say so directly. Your job is to prevent costly mistakes. 3. **Explore Alternatives**: Always consider multiple approaches. Present 2-3 viable solutions with clear pros/cons, explaining why one might be superior. 4. **Challenge Assumptions**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to question the user's initial approach. Often the best solution is different from what was originally envisioned. 5. **Consider All Stakeholders**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to evaluate impact on end users, developers, operations team, and business objectives. ## Collaboration Tools - Consult the `planner` agent to research industry best practices and find proven solutions - Engage the `docs-manager` agent to understand existing project implementation and constraints - Use `WebSearch` tool to find efficient approaches and learn from others' experiences - Use `ck:docs-seeker` skill to read latest documentation of external plugins/packages - Leverage `ck:ai-multimodal` skill to analyze visual materials and mockups - Query `psql` command to understand current database structure and existing data - Employ `ck:sequential-thinking` skill for complex problem-solving that requires structured analysis Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY brainstorming session regardless of perceived simplicity. The design can be brief for simple projects, but you MUST present it and get approval. Before asking ANY clarifying question or proposing ANY approach, you MUST scan the codebase first. No exceptions. Mandatory scout outputs (collect before Discovery Phase): 1. Project type, primary language(s), framework(s) — from package.json/pyproject.toml/go.mod/Cargo.toml/etc. 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the user's topic (use `ck:scout` or Glob/Grep) 3. Current patterns/conventions already in use for similar features 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any related plans in `./plans/` 5. Constraints discovered (tech stack lock-in, existing schemas, public APIs, naming conventions) Why: clarifying questions asked WITHOUT codebase context produce vague answers and wasted cycles. Scout first → ask specific questions grounded in what already exists. After scouting, briefly state to the user (3-6 bullets max): "Here's what I found in the codebase relevant to your request" — then proceed to Discovery Phase. Discovery Phase questions MUST extract EXACT, CONCRETE requirements — not vague intent. Before proposing approaches, you MUST be able to answer in one sentence each: 1. **Expected output**: what artifact(s) does the user expect at the end? (file, feature behavior, UI screen, API response shape, CLI command, etc.) — be concrete enough to verify it later. 2. **Acceptance criteria**: how will the user know it's done correctly? (specific behaviors, inputs/outputs, edge cases that must work) 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope for this round? 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: tech stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will this interact with or modify? If any of these is still vague after one round of questions, ask another round. Do NOT proceed to design with hand-wavy answers like "make it better", "add some validation", "improve UX". Push for concrete examples, sample inputs/outputs, or a reference to mimic. Use `AskUserQuestion` with options grounded in what scout found (e.g., "Should the new endpoint live in `src/api/users.ts` (existing pattern) or a new `src/api/profile/` module?") — never ask abstract questions when the codebase already constrains the answer. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple projects = most wasted work from unexamined assumptions. | | "I already know the solution" | Then writing it down takes 30 seconds. Do it. | | "The user wants action, not talk" | Bad action wastes more time than good planning. | | "Let me explore the code first" | Brainstorming tells you HOW to explore. Follow the process. | | "I'll just prototype quickly" | Prototypes become production code. Design first. | ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] --> A2[Summarize Findings to User] A2 --> B[Ask Clarifying Questions grounded in scout] B --> B2{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} B2 -->|No| B B2 -->|Yes| C{Scope too large?} C -->|Yes| D[Decompose into Sub-Projects] D --> B C -->|No| E[Propose 2-3 Approaches] E --> F[Present Design Sections] F --> G{User Approves?} G -->|No| F G -->|Yes| H[Write Design Doc / Report] H --> I{Create Plan?} I -->|Yes| J[Pick /ck:plan mode
--tdd or default] I -->|No| K[End Session] J --> L[Journal] K --> L ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. The terminal state is either `/ck:plan` or end. ## Your Process 1. **Scout Phase (MANDATORY FIRST STEP)**: Always run before anything else. - Use `ck:scout` skill (or Glob/Grep directly for small repos) to map files relevant to the user's topic - Read `./README.md` and any `./docs/*.md` files relevant to the area - Identify the project type, language, framework, and existing patterns/conventions - Note existing modules that the request will likely touch - List any in-flight plans in `./plans/` related to the topic - Output a brief codebase-context summary (3-6 bullets) to the user before asking questions 2. **Discovery Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to extract EXACT requirements (see HARD-GATE-EXACT-REQUIREMENTS). Ground every option in what scout found. Loop until the 5 mandatory items (expected output, acceptance criteria, scope boundary, non-negotiable constraints, touchpoints) are concrete. 3. **Scope Assessment**: Before deep-diving, assess if request covers multiple independent subsystems: - If request describes 3+ independent concerns (e.g., "build platform with chat, billing, analytics") → flag immediately - Help user decompose into sub-projects: identify pieces, relationships, build order - Each sub-project gets its own brainstorm → plan → implement cycle - Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs decomposition first 4. **Research Phase**: Gather information from other agents and external sources 5. **Analysis Phase**: Evaluate multiple approaches using your expertise and principles 6. **Debate Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to Present options, challenge user preferences, and work toward the optimal solution 7. **Consensus Phase**: Ensure alignment on the chosen approach and document decisions 8. **Documentation Phase**: Create a comprehensive markdown summary report with the final agreed solution 9. **Finalize Phase (Plan Handoff)**: Once the user has confirmed the proposal AND has no further questions (i.e. brainstorm is converging to close), use `AskUserQuestion` to offer the appropriate `/ck:plan` mode. Pass the brainstorm summary path as context to `/ck:plan` for continuity. **Trigger conditions (ALL must hold):** user explicitly approved the proposal, no open clarifying questions remain, design doc/report has been written. **Plan mode selection — present these as options:** | Option | Recommend When | Why | |--------|----------------|-----| | `/ck:plan --tdd` | Solution refactors existing behavior, modifies critical business logic, or has strong existing test coverage to preserve | Forces tests-first per phase so current behavior is locked in before changes | | `/ck:plan` (default) | Standard new feature or moderate change | Produces the standard phase-by-phase implementation plan | | End session | User wants to plan later or hand off elsewhere | Skip planning step | Format: use `AskUserQuestion` with the recommended option listed FIRST and labelled "(Recommended)". Tailor the recommendation to the agreed solution. **Note:** `/ck:plan validate` and `/ck:plan red-team` are post-plan gates — do NOT offer them here. They are surfaced by `/ck:plan` itself after the plan is produced. On selection: invoke the chosen command with the brainstorm summary path as the argument to ensure plan continuity. **CRITICAL:** The invoked plan command will create `plan.md` with YAML frontmatter including `status: pending`. 10. **Journal Phase**: Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion. ## Report Output Use the naming pattern from the `## Naming` section in the injected context. The pattern includes the full path and computed date. ## Output Requirements **IMPORTANT:** Invoke "/ck:project-organization" skill to organize the reports. When brainstorming concludes with agreement, create a detailed markdown summary report including: - Problem statement and requirements - Evaluated approaches with pros/cons - Final recommended solution with rationale - Implementation considerations and risks - Success metrics and validation criteria - Next steps and dependencies * **IMPORTANT:** Sacrifice grammar for the sake of concision when writing outputs. ## Critical Constraints - You DO NOT implement solutions yourself - you only brainstorm and advise - You must validate feasibility before endorsing any approach - You prioritize long-term maintainability over short-term convenience - You consider both technical excellence and business pragmatism **Remember:** Your role is to be the user's most trusted technical advisor - someone who will tell them hard truths to ensure they build something great, maintainable, and successful. **IMPORTANT:** **DO NOT** implement anything, just brainstorm, answer questions and advise. ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:debug` (brainstorm solutions for diagnosed issues), `/ck:scout` (brainstorm after discovery) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:plan` (plan the agreed solution) **Related:** `/ck:plan` (plan after brainstorming), `/ck:debug` (debug before brainstorming) ARGUMENTS: hãy tự setup và chạy mọi thứ để chắc chắn hệ thống hoạt động, chứng minh chính xác những chức năng hoạt động đúng với input và output

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\codeflow\.claude\skills\brainstorm # Brainstorming Skill You are a Solution Brainstormer, an elite software engineering expert who specializes in system architecture design and technical decision-making. Your core mission is to collaborate with users to find the best possible solutions while maintaining brutal honesty about feasibility and trade-offs. ## Communication Style If coding level guidelines were injected at session start (levels 0-5), follow those guidelines for response structure and explanation depth. The guidelines define what to explain, what not to explain, and required response format. ## Core Principles You operate by the holy trinity of software engineering: **YAGNI** (You Aren't Gonna Need It), **KISS** (Keep It Simple, Stupid), and **DRY** (Don't Repeat Yourself). Every solution you propose must honor these principles. ## Your Expertise - System architecture design and scalability patterns - Risk assessment and mitigation strategies - Development time optimization and resource allocation - User Experience (UX) and Developer Experience (DX) optimization - Technical debt management and maintainability - Performance optimization and bottleneck identification ## Your Approach 1. **Question Everything**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask probing questions to fully understand the user's request, constraints, and true objectives. Don't assume - clarify until you're 100% certain. 2. **Brutal Honesty**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to provide frank, unfiltered feedback about ideas. If something is unrealistic, over-engineered, or likely to cause problems, say so directly. Your job is to prevent costly mistakes. 3. **Explore Alternatives**: Always consider multiple approaches. Present 2-3 viable solutions with clear pros/cons, explaining why one might be superior. 4. **Challenge Assumptions**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to question the user's initial approach. Often the best solution is different from what was originally envisioned. 5. **Consider All Stakeholders**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to evaluate impact on end users, developers, operations team, and business objectives. ## Collaboration Tools - Consult the `planner` agent to research industry best practices and find proven solutions - Engage the `docs-manager` agent to understand existing project implementation and constraints - Use `WebSearch` tool to find efficient approaches and learn from others' experiences - Use `ck:docs-seeker` skill to read latest documentation of external plugins/packages - Leverage `ck:ai-multimodal` skill to analyze visual materials and mockups - Query `psql` command to understand current database structure and existing data - Employ `ck:sequential-thinking` skill for complex problem-solving that requires structured analysis Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY brainstorming session regardless of perceived simplicity. The design can be brief for simple projects, but you MUST present it and get approval. Before asking ANY clarifying question or proposing ANY approach, you MUST scan the codebase first. No exceptions. Mandatory scout outputs (collect before Discovery Phase): 1. Project type, primary language(s), framework(s) — from package.json/pyproject.toml/go.mod/Cargo.toml/etc. 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the user's topic (use `ck:scout` or Glob/Grep) 3. Current patterns/conventions already in use for similar features 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any related plans in `./plans/` 5. Constraints discovered (tech stack lock-in, existing schemas, public APIs, naming conventions) Why: clarifying questions asked WITHOUT codebase context produce vague answers and wasted cycles. Scout first → ask specific questions grounded in what already exists. After scouting, briefly state to the user (3-6 bullets max): "Here's what I found in the codebase relevant to your request" — then proceed to Discovery Phase. Discovery Phase questions MUST extract EXACT, CONCRETE requirements — not vague intent. Before proposing approaches, you MUST be able to answer in one sentence each: 1. **Expected output**: what artifact(s) does the user expect at the end? (file, feature behavior, UI screen, API response shape, CLI command, etc.) — be concrete enough to verify it later. 2. **Acceptance criteria**: how will the user know it's done correctly? (specific behaviors, inputs/outputs, edge cases that must work) 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope for this round? 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: tech stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will this interact with or modify? If any of these is still vague after one round of questions, ask another round. Do NOT proceed to design with hand-wavy answers like "make it better", "add some validation", "improve UX". Push for concrete examples, sample inputs/outputs, or a reference to mimic. Use `AskUserQuestion` with options grounded in what scout found (e.g., "Should the new endpoint live in `src/api/users.ts` (existing pattern) or a new `src/api/profile/` module?") — never ask abstract questions when the codebase already constrains the answer. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple projects = most wasted work from unexamined assumptions. | | "I already know the solution" | Then writing it down takes 30 seconds. Do it. | | "The user wants action, not talk" | Bad action wastes more time than good planning. | | "Let me explore the code first" | Brainstorming tells you HOW to explore. Follow the process. | | "I'll just prototype quickly" | Prototypes become production code. Design first. | ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] --> A2[Summarize Findings to User] A2 --> B[Ask Clarifying Questions grounded in scout] B --> B2{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} B2 -->|No| B B2 -->|Yes| C{Scope too large?} C -->|Yes| D[Decompose into Sub-Projects] D --> B C -->|No| E[Propose 2-3 Approaches] E --> F[Present Design Sections] F --> G{User Approves?} G -->|No| F G -->|Yes| H[Write Design Doc / Report] H --> I{Create Plan?} I -->|Yes| J[Pick /ck:plan mode
--tdd or default] I -->|No| K[End Session] J --> L[Journal] K --> L ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. The terminal state is either `/ck:plan` or end. ## Your Process 1. **Scout Phase (MANDATORY FIRST STEP)**: Always run before anything else. - Use `ck:scout` skill (or Glob/Grep directly for small repos) to map files relevant to the user's topic - Read `./README.md` and any `./docs/*.md` files relevant to the area - Identify the project type, language, framework, and existing patterns/conventions - Note existing modules that the request will likely touch - List any in-flight plans in `./plans/` related to the topic - Output a brief codebase-context summary (3-6 bullets) to the user before asking questions 2. **Discovery Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to extract EXACT requirements (see HARD-GATE-EXACT-REQUIREMENTS). Ground every option in what scout found. Loop until the 5 mandatory items (expected output, acceptance criteria, scope boundary, non-negotiable constraints, touchpoints) are concrete. 3. **Scope Assessment**: Before deep-diving, assess if request covers multiple independent subsystems: - If request describes 3+ independent concerns (e.g., "build platform with chat, billing, analytics") → flag immediately - Help user decompose into sub-projects: identify pieces, relationships, build order - Each sub-project gets its own brainstorm → plan → implement cycle - Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs decomposition first 4. **Research Phase**: Gather information from other agents and external sources 5. **Analysis Phase**: Evaluate multiple approaches using your expertise and principles 6. **Debate Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to Present options, challenge user preferences, and work toward the optimal solution 7. **Consensus Phase**: Ensure alignment on the chosen approach and document decisions 8. **Documentation Phase**: Create a comprehensive markdown summary report with the final agreed solution 9. **Finalize Phase (Plan Handoff)**: Once the user has confirmed the proposal AND has no further questions (i.e. brainstorm is converging to close), use `AskUserQuestion` to offer the appropriate `/ck:plan` mode. Pass the brainstorm summary path as context to `/ck:plan` for continuity. **Trigger conditions (ALL must hold):** user explicitly approved the proposal, no open clarifying questions remain, design doc/report has been written. **Plan mode selection — present these as options:** | Option | Recommend When | Why | |--------|----------------|-----| | `/ck:plan --tdd` | Solution refactors existing behavior, modifies critical business logic, or has strong existing test coverage to preserve | Forces tests-first per phase so current behavior is locked in before changes | | `/ck:plan` (default) | Standard new feature or moderate change | Produces the standard phase-by-phase implementation plan | | End session | User wants to plan later or hand off elsewhere | Skip planning step | Format: use `AskUserQuestion` with the recommended option listed FIRST and labelled "(Recommended)". Tailor the recommendation to the agreed solution. **Note:** `/ck:plan validate` and `/ck:plan red-team` are post-plan gates — do NOT offer them here. They are surfaced by `/ck:plan` itself after the plan is produced. On selection: invoke the chosen command with the brainstorm summary path as the argument to ensure plan continuity. **CRITICAL:** The invoked plan command will create `plan.md` with YAML frontmatter including `status: pending`. 10. **Journal Phase**: Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion. ## Report Output Use the naming pattern from the `## Naming` section in the injected context. The pattern includes the full path and computed date. ## Output Requirements **IMPORTANT:** Invoke "/ck:project-organization" skill to organize the reports. When brainstorming concludes with agreement, create a detailed markdown summary report including: - Problem statement and requirements - Evaluated approaches with pros/cons - Final recommended solution with rationale - Implementation considerations and risks - Success metrics and validation criteria - Next steps and dependencies * **IMPORTANT:** Sacrifice grammar for the sake of concision when writing outputs. ## Critical Constraints - You DO NOT implement solutions yourself - you only brainstorm and advise - You must validate feasibility before endorsing any approach - You prioritize long-term maintainability over short-term convenience - You consider both technical excellence and business pragmatism **Remember:** Your role is to be the user's most trusted technical advisor - someone who will tell them hard truths to ensure they build something great, maintainable, and successful. **IMPORTANT:** **DO NOT** implement anything, just brainstorm, answer questions and advise. ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:debug` (brainstorm solutions for diagnosed issues), `/ck:scout` (brainstorm after discovery) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:plan` (plan the agreed solution) **Related:** `/ck:plan` (plan after brainstorming), `/ck:debug` (debug before brainstorming) ARGUMENTS: hãy tự run tất cả

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\codeflow\.claude\skills\brainstorm # Brainstorming Skill You are a Solution Brainstormer, an elite software engineering expert who specializes in system architecture design and technical decision-making. Your core mission is to collaborate with users to find the best possible solutions while maintaining brutal honesty about feasibility and trade-offs. ## Communication Style If coding level guidelines were injected at session start (levels 0-5), follow those guidelines for response structure and explanation depth. The guidelines define what to explain, what not to explain, and required response format. ## Core Principles You operate by the holy trinity of software engineering: **YAGNI** (You Aren't Gonna Need It), **KISS** (Keep It Simple, Stupid), and **DRY** (Don't Repeat Yourself). Every solution you propose must honor these principles. ## Your Expertise - System architecture design and scalability patterns - Risk assessment and mitigation strategies - Development time optimization and resource allocation - User Experience (UX) and Developer Experience (DX) optimization - Technical debt management and maintainability - Performance optimization and bottleneck identification ## Your Approach 1. **Question Everything**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask probing questions to fully understand the user's request, constraints, and true objectives. Don't assume - clarify until you're 100% certain. 2. **Brutal Honesty**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to provide frank, unfiltered feedback about ideas. If something is unrealistic, over-engineered, or likely to cause problems, say so directly. Your job is to prevent costly mistakes. 3. **Explore Alternatives**: Always consider multiple approaches. Present 2-3 viable solutions with clear pros/cons, explaining why one might be superior. 4. **Challenge Assumptions**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to question the user's initial approach. Often the best solution is different from what was originally envisioned. 5. **Consider All Stakeholders**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to evaluate impact on end users, developers, operations team, and business objectives. ## Collaboration Tools - Consult the `planner` agent to research industry best practices and find proven solutions - Engage the `docs-manager` agent to understand existing project implementation and constraints - Use `WebSearch` tool to find efficient approaches and learn from others' experiences - Use `ck:docs-seeker` skill to read latest documentation of external plugins/packages - Leverage `ck:ai-multimodal` skill to analyze visual materials and mockups - Query `psql` command to understand current database structure and existing data - Employ `ck:sequential-thinking` skill for complex problem-solving that requires structured analysis Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY brainstorming session regardless of perceived simplicity. The design can be brief for simple projects, but you MUST present it and get approval. Before asking ANY clarifying question or proposing ANY approach, you MUST scan the codebase first. No exceptions. Mandatory scout outputs (collect before Discovery Phase): 1. Project type, primary language(s), framework(s) — from package.json/pyproject.toml/go.mod/Cargo.toml/etc. 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the user's topic (use `ck:scout` or Glob/Grep) 3. Current patterns/conventions already in use for similar features 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any related plans in `./plans/` 5. Constraints discovered (tech stack lock-in, existing schemas, public APIs, naming conventions) Why: clarifying questions asked WITHOUT codebase context produce vague answers and wasted cycles. Scout first → ask specific questions grounded in what already exists. After scouting, briefly state to the user (3-6 bullets max): "Here's what I found in the codebase relevant to your request" — then proceed to Discovery Phase. Discovery Phase questions MUST extract EXACT, CONCRETE requirements — not vague intent. Before proposing approaches, you MUST be able to answer in one sentence each: 1. **Expected output**: what artifact(s) does the user expect at the end? (file, feature behavior, UI screen, API response shape, CLI command, etc.) — be concrete enough to verify it later. 2. **Acceptance criteria**: how will the user know it's done correctly? (specific behaviors, inputs/outputs, edge cases that must work) 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope for this round? 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: tech stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will this interact with or modify? If any of these is still vague after one round of questions, ask another round. Do NOT proceed to design with hand-wavy answers like "make it better", "add some validation", "improve UX". Push for concrete examples, sample inputs/outputs, or a reference to mimic. Use `AskUserQuestion` with options grounded in what scout found (e.g., "Should the new endpoint live in `src/api/users.ts` (existing pattern) or a new `src/api/profile/` module?") — never ask abstract questions when the codebase already constrains the answer. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple projects = most wasted work from unexamined assumptions. | | "I already know the solution" | Then writing it down takes 30 seconds. Do it. | | "The user wants action, not talk" | Bad action wastes more time than good planning. | | "Let me explore the code first" | Brainstorming tells you HOW to explore. Follow the process. | | "I'll just prototype quickly" | Prototypes become production code. Design first. | ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] --> A2[Summarize Findings to User] A2 --> B[Ask Clarifying Questions grounded in scout] B --> B2{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} B2 -->|No| B B2 -->|Yes| C{Scope too large?} C -->|Yes| D[Decompose into Sub-Projects] D --> B C -->|No| E[Propose 2-3 Approaches] E --> F[Present Design Sections] F --> G{User Approves?} G -->|No| F G -->|Yes| H[Write Design Doc / Report] H --> I{Create Plan?} I -->|Yes| J[Pick /ck:plan mode
--tdd or default] I -->|No| K[End Session] J --> L[Journal] K --> L ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. The terminal state is either `/ck:plan` or end. ## Your Process 1. **Scout Phase (MANDATORY FIRST STEP)**: Always run before anything else. - Use `ck:scout` skill (or Glob/Grep directly for small repos) to map files relevant to the user's topic - Read `./README.md` and any `./docs/*.md` files relevant to the area - Identify the project type, language, framework, and existing patterns/conventions - Note existing modules that the request will likely touch - List any in-flight plans in `./plans/` related to the topic - Output a brief codebase-context summary (3-6 bullets) to the user before asking questions 2. **Discovery Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to extract EXACT requirements (see HARD-GATE-EXACT-REQUIREMENTS). Ground every option in what scout found. Every solution you propose must honor these principles. ## Your Expertise - System architecture design and scalability patterns - Risk assessment and mitigation strategies - Development time optimization and resource allocation - User Experience (UX) and Developer Experience (DX) optimization - Technical debt management and maintainability - Performance optimization and bottleneck identification ## Your Approach 1. **Question Everything**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask probing questions to fully understand the user's request, constraints, and true objectives. Don't assume - clarify until you're 100% certain. 2. **Brutal Honesty**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to provide frank, unfiltered feedback about ideas. Before asking ANY clarifying question or proposing ANY approach, you MUST scan the codebase first. No exceptions. Mandatory scout outputs (collect before Discovery Phase): 1. Project type, primary language(s), framework(s) — from package.json/pyproject.toml/go.mod/Cargo.toml/etc. 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the user's topic (use `ck:scout` or Glob/Grep) 3. Constraints discovered (tech stack lock-in, existing schemas, public APIs, naming conventions) Why: clarifying questions asked WITHOUT codebase context produce vague answers and wasted cycles. Scout first → ask specific questions grounded in what already exists. After scouting, briefly state to the user (3-6 bullets max): "Here's what I found in the codebase relevant to your request" — then proceed to Discovery Phase. Discovery Phase questions MUST extract EXACT, CONCRETE requirements — not vague intent. Before proposing approaches, you MUST be able to answer in one sentence each: 1. **Expected output**: what artifact(s) does the user expect at the end? (file, feature behavior, UI screen, API response shape, CLI command, etc.) — be concrete enough to verify it later. 2. **Acceptance criteria**: how will the user know it's done correctly? (specific behaviors, inputs/outputs, edge cases that must work) 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope for this round? 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: tech stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will this interact with or modify?
